overview: The Multimodal Logistics Park (MMLP) Scheme is a government initiative aimed at developing integrated logistics infrastructure to enhance freight movement efficiency across India. It focuses on creating multimodal hubs that connect various transport modes such as road, rail, and waterways to reduce logistics costs and improve supply chain performance. The scheme is implemented by NHIDCL under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and supports the Bharatmala Pariyojana and Act East Policy objectives. MMLPs are envisioned as key enablers for economic growth in strategic regions, particularly the North Eastern Region and border areas.
objectives: Develop integrated multimodal logistics infrastructure to reduce logistics costs
Enhance connectivity between road, rail, and inland waterways for seamless freight movement
Support the Act East Policy by improving regional connectivity in the North Eastern Region
Promote economic growth in remote and strategic regions through improved infrastructure
Facilitate international trade by strengthening links with neighbouring countries
Develop automated parking, multi-modal logistics parks, and bus ports as part of IT-enabled infrastructure
Act as a nodal agency for infrastructure development in border and international connectivity roads
eligibility: Entities involved in logistics, transport, warehousing, or industrial operations seeking to establish or upgrade multimodal logistics parks in India, particularly in the North Eastern Region, border areas, and strategic corridors under Bharatmala Pariyojana, are eligible to participate or benefit from the scheme through collaboration with NHIDCL.
benefits: The MMLP Scheme offers benefits such as reduced logistics costs, improved supply chain efficiency, enhanced regional connectivity, better access to national and international markets, support for industrial development, job creation in logistics and allied sectors, and integration with digital platforms like INAMPRO, INFRACON, and ePACE for transparent operations. It also enables private sector participation through PPP models and facilitates access to funding from global institutions like ADB and JICA.
financial_support: Financial support under the MMLP Scheme is structured through public-private partnership (PPP) models, with funding sourced from government budgetary allocations, loans from financial institutions, and investments from global agencies such as the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). NHIDCL facilitates project structuring and implementation, leveraging its expertise in infrastructure development in challenging terrains.
application_process: 1. Identify a suitable location for the Multimodal Logistics Park (MMLP) in alignment with national logistics plans and regional connectivity goals. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) including technical, financial, and environmental aspects. 3. Submit the proposal to NHIDCL or the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways for appraisal. 4. Obtain necessary clearances and approvals from relevant authorities. 5. Enter into a concession agreement or MoU with NHIDCL for project execution. 6. Proceed with land acquisition, design, and construction as per approved plans. 7. Commission the MMLP and initiate operations under the agreed operational framework.
required_documents: No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from relevant departments
Incorporation documents of the applicant entity
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Proposals are accepted and evaluated periodically based on fund availability and project readiness.
implementing_agency: National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL), under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Government of India
caveats: Projects must align with national logistics plans and Bharatmala Pariyojana objectives
Priority is given to projects in the North Eastern Region, border areas, and strategic corridors
Private sector participation is encouraged through PPP models
Environmental and social safeguards must be complied with during implementation
Land acquisition and statutory clearances are the responsibility of the project developer
